blocks.orig: 10 DAYS SAFARI MIKUMI + UDZUNGWA + RUAHA + NYERERE
blocks.html: 10-day safari through Mikumi, Udzungwa, Ruaha and Nyerere

blocks.orig: This is a perfect safari combination to visit the southern national parks in Tanzania.
blocks.html: If you want to see the national parks of southern Tanzania, this combination of safaris suits you well.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park has a great variety of animals such as the Big Five and chances that you will encounter lions climbing up trees is higher here than in other parks! Udzungwa National Park is known for sightings of the rare Iringa red colobus monkey and the Sanje crested mangabey. You can find these two types only in this region. The park has the second-largest biodiversity of any national park in Africa. And Ruaha National Park is not only the second-largest park, but is probably home to more elephants than any other national park in East Africa. Nyerere National Park  (previously Selous Game Reserve) is Tanzania’s largest park. Due to its wildlife diversity and undisturbed nature, it is even a UNESCO World Heritage Site!
blocks.html: In Mikumi National Park you find a wide range of wildlife, the Big Five included, and your odds of seeing lions up in the trees are better here than in other parks! Udzungwa National Park is where people come to see the rare Iringa red colobus monkey and the Sanje crested mangabey, two species that live only in this region. No national park in Africa except one has greater biodiversity. Then there is Ruaha National Park: the second-largest park, and quite possibly the one with more elephants than any other national park in East Africa. Nyerere National Park  (formerly the Selous Game Reserve) is the largest park in Tanzania. Thanks to its varied wildlife and untouched nature, it has even been named a UNESCO World Heritage Site!

blocks.orig: This private safari offers you the flexibility to travel at your own pace, exactly the way you like it. You will have a private safari vehicle and guide.
blocks.html: With this private safari you set your own pace and travel exactly as you prefer. A safari vehicle and a guide are reserved just for you.

blocks.orig: NOTE: Udzungwa is offering only a small choice of accommodations, and these are very basic. Although we give you options for Gold and Platinum hotels for this route, these DON’T apply for Udzungwa!
blocks.html: PLEASE NOTE: the choice of places to stay in Udzungwa is small, and the options are very simple. We do list Gold and Platinum hotels for this route, but those categories DON’T cover Udzungwa!

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear from many travellers is when to go to Tanzania. The honest reply … no single answer fits everyone. It comes down to what you hope to see, the places you want to visit, your budget and your interests. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: On a safari with us in Tanzania you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our focus, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is for you alone. You decide when each safari day begins and finishes, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you choose. Perhaps you would like to see the animals at their liveliest around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or perhaps you would rather finish the afternoon at the pool; the choice is completely yours. Because the wildlife of Tanzania is active at different moments of the day, you’ll get many chances to watch the animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely: Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals (lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo) in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country to travel in. You’ll find a welcoming atmosphere, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can enjoy the scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are kind, and simple precautions like keeping an eye on your belongings remain sensible, as they would be anywhere in the world. With its natural beauty and warm-hearted people, Tanzania is a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.html: Welcome to Tanzania! When you land at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly guide, who knows the country well, will be there waiting to greet you. He is on hand to help you and makes sure your transfer to the hotel goes smoothly. Lean back and relax while we look after everything you need for the journey, so your time in Tanzania becomes a memorable experience.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park lies at a six-hour drive from Dar Es Salaam and is Tanzania's fourth largest national park. The open horizons and abundant wildlife draw frequent comparisons to the more famous Serengeti plains, but its location close to Tanzania's largest city makes Mikumi easier accessible. The park has a great variety of animals: elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes are relatively easy to spot, as well as lions mating and many hippos in the resident hippo pool!
blocks.html: Six hours by road from Dar Es Salaam, you reach Mikumi National Park, the fourth largest national park in Tanzania. Its wide horizons and plentiful wildlife are often compared with the better-known Serengeti plains, yet because it sits near Tanzania's largest city, Mikumi is easier to get to. The range of animals is broad: you can spot elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes fairly easily, plus mating lions and plenty of hippos in the resident hippo pool!

blocks.orig: Udzungwa Mountains National Park is a relatively small, mountainous national park, known for its rare endemic species. In this tropical rainforest, you encounter bush elephants, monkeys, several smaller mammals, and over 400 bird species. Animals that can only be found here are primates such as the red Iringa Colobus and the Sanje Crested Mangabey. But also the grey-faced sengi (an elephant shrew) is endemic to Udzungwa as are several remarkable bird species.
blocks.html: Udzungwa Mountains National Park is fairly small and mountainous, and it is famous for rare endemic species. This tropical rainforest is home to bush elephants, monkeys, a number of smaller mammals and more than 400 bird species. Some primates live nowhere else, such as the red Iringa Colobus and the Sanje Crested Mangabey. The grey-faced sengi (an elephant shrew) is also endemic to Udzungwa, and so are a number of notable bird species.

blocks.orig: There are no paved roads in this national park, which means it’s perfect for shorter and longer hikes. The four-hour hike to the Sanje waterfalls is both challenging and refreshing, as you hike up the mountain but can reward yourself with a plunge at the bottom of the waterfall. Along the way, you might just spot one of those rare monkeys in the trees or see elephant tracks (of so-called mountain elephants). Keep in mind that it can be hot during midday, but if you stay in the shade and hydrated, this is a great walk!
blocks.html: With no paved roads inside the park, it is ideal for both short and long hikes. The four-hour walk to the Sanje waterfalls is tough as well as refreshing: you climb the mountain, and at the foot of the waterfall you can treat yourself to a swim. On the way you may see one of those rare monkeys in the trees, or come across elephant tracks (left by the so-called mountain elephants). Bear in mind that midday can be hot, but if you keep to the shade and drink enough, it is a lovely walk!

blocks.orig: Ruaha National Park is the third largest national park in Tanzania. It lies along the Great Ruaha River, is known for its large elephant population, and is a true paradise for birdwatchers with over 570 species. Besides, you might catch a glimpse of lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals, or the rare African wild dog. Game drives are special, as you drive through an untouched ecosystem in this relatively quiet but stunning park!
blocks.html: Tanzania's third largest national park is Ruaha National Park. Set along the Great Ruaha River, it is known for its big elephant population, and with more than 570 species it is a real haven for birdwatchers. You may also get to see lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals or the rare African wild dog. The game drives feel special, because you travel through an unspoilt ecosystem in a park that is fairly quiet yet beautiful!

blocks.orig: Fly to Nyerere National Park and experience the breathtaking beauty of Tanzania's diverse wildlife and landscapes. Explore the vast plains, dense forests, and meandering rivers on exhilarating wildlife safaris, discover the iconic "Big Five," and witness the impressive wildebeest migration. Embark on this safari adventure and create unforgettable memories amidst the untamed wilderness of Nyerere National Park.
blocks.html: Take a flight to Nyerere National Park and take in the stunning variety of Tanzania's wildlife and scenery. On exciting wildlife safaris you explore wide plains, thick forests and winding rivers, look for the well-known "Big Five" and see the remarkable wildebeest migration. Set out on this safari and collect memories you will not forget in the wild nature of Nyerere National Park.

blocks.orig: During a boat safari of 2 - 3 hours, you discover the scenic Rufiji River and its animals. From the boat, you might spot hippos, crocodiles, monkeys, many birds AND a beautiful sunset! For this sunset, you set foot on one of the small sandbanks on the river, where you can stretch your legs or enjoy a drink while the sun sets in this magical environment. There is nothing more beautiful than the serenity of a river completely surrounded by nature at this golden hour of the day.
blocks.html: On a boat safari lasting 2 - 3 hours, you explore the beautiful Rufiji River and the animals along it. You may see hippos, crocodiles, monkeys and many birds from the boat, AND a lovely sunset! To watch it, you step onto one of the little sandbanks in the river, where you can stretch your legs or have a drink as the sun goes down in this magical setting. Few things are as beautiful as the calm of a river surrounded entirely by nature during this golden hour of the day.

blocks.orig: Today you discover the jungle, savannah and river sides of the vast Nyerere National Park (previously the Selous Game Reserve) - an amazing place for game drives. This park in southern Tanzania has fewer visitors than the northern parks but boasts elephants, hippos, crocodiles, lions, leopards, giraffes, the endangered rhino, the rare African wild dog and more. It's the second largest park in the country after Serengeti National Park, so be prepared to cover some miles!
blocks.html: Today is about exploring the jungle, savannah and riverbanks of the huge Nyerere National Park (formerly the Selous Game Reserve), a superb spot for game drives. Fewer people visit this park in southern Tanzania than the northern parks, yet it has elephants, hippos, crocodiles, lions, leopards, giraffes, the endangered rhino, the rare African wild dog and more. After Serengeti National Park it is the second largest park in the country, so expect to cover quite a few miles!

blocks.orig: This is your last day! Today you fly to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam, from where you will catch your international flight home. Having second thoughts? Then don't hesitate to extend your holiday to one of Tanzania's paradise islands such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day has arrived! You fly today to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam, where your international flight home departs. Not ready to leave yet? Then feel free to add a few days on one of Tanzania's tropical islands such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
